facts.raw_span: painful swelling of the proximal nail folds
dripping of blood from his fingernails and toenails for the last year
occasional pus discharge
no history of preceding trauma or drug intake
lichenoid plaques on the right angle of mouth, bilateral buccal mucosa, and erosions covered with hemorrhagic crusts on the upper and lower lips
violaceous discoloration of 7 fingernails and 3 toenails
longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate
partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood resulting in hemorrhagic crusting of the nail beds and folds
raised liver enzyme levels
positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status
Hyperkeratosis, Hypergranulosis, Acanthosis, Basal cell degeneration, Numerous apoptotic keratinocytes in the epidermis, Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis
Swelling and violaceous discoloration on the proximal fingernail folds along with oozing of blood, hemorrhagic crusting of the fingernails, and pus discharging from the lateral nail folds

concepts.why: The patient has a positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status.
The patient presents with violaceous discoloration, longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate, which are characteristic of nail psoriasis.
The patient has lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, which is a characteristic feature of oral lichen planus.
The patient presents with nail changes, including longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate, which can be seen in nail lichen planus.
The patient has a positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status and presents with features of lichen planus, including oral and nail involvement.
It explains the histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, basal cell degeneration, and dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis.

rationales.F05: Lichenoid plaques and erosions are characteristic of oral lichen planus
rationales.F10: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status is a strong indicator of hepatitis C virus infection
rationales.F11: Histopathological findings are consistent with lichen planus

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status and symptoms consistent with lichen planus, such as lichenoid plaques and violaceous discoloration of the nails, support the diagnosis of Hepatitis C virus-associated lichen planus.
